idiom_name: kotlinx.serialization @Serializable DTOs with a configured Json format (compiler-plugin generated serializers)
implementation_notes: The contract is bound by the compiler plugin rather than by reflection: mark wire DTOs @Serializable, pin the published names with @SerialName, configure the format to match the documented policy - Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true; explicitNulls = false } - and encode/decode with Json.encodeToString()/decodeFromString(). Schema-first contracts use protoc --kotlin_out generated messages over the same .proto as every other runtime. Hand-written mappers are still justified when the published shape differs materially from the domain model, because kotlinx.serialization binds equal shapes and does not translate semantics.
pitfalls: ignoreUnknownKeys defaults to false: without it a producer adding a field breaks every consumer, which contradicts the evolution policy a published language normally promises.
A missing non-null property raises MissingFieldException; giving every field a default hides schema violations behind plausible wrong data instead.
The generated serializer follows the class shape, so renaming or reordering properties is a wire change unless @SerialName pins the published names.
